reviewed_by: Static review of the retail instruction sequence (radare2 disassembly, Binary Ninja + angr CFG) against the corrected candidate source
reviewed_scope: engine/src/retail/script/humanplayer_defines.cpp lines 34-121 and the declarations in humanplayer_defines.hpp

checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Radare2 (5 blocks/6 edges, 326 bytes, cdecl), the existing Binary Ninja record (5 nodes/6 edges) and angr CFGFast (nodes 0x00410070-0x004101AF) agree on the entry and the two table loops; the candidate implements that entry.

checks.name: abi_and_arguments
checks.rationale: The body reads the argument frame from [esp+0x34] at 0x00410075 (third stack argument) and the result block pointer from [esp+0x30] at 0x0041017E (first stack argument); the second stack argument is never read. The candidate takes (void* context, int32_t argument_slot, void* frame), documents the unused slot and returns the context pointer in EAX, which is what the native-call site 0x004BD8FE copies from.

checks.name: argument_series
checks.rationale: Retail calls 0x004B8A50 exactly 43 times: indices 0..8 in the straight-line part, 9..25 in the 0x00410145 walk and 26..42 in the 0x00410164 walk. The candidate performs the same 43 reads in the same index order.

checks.name: scaling_and_constants
checks.rationale: Indices 0, 7 and 8 are stored raw; 1..3 are multiplied by the float 4096000.0 at 0x005334A4 (0x4A7A0000) and then by the float at 0x005334A0 (0x371B5837 = 9.259259059035685e-06) in x87 80-bit arithmetic; 4 and 5 are multiplied by the double 4096.0 at 0x00533498; 6 is multiplied by the double 30.0 at 0x00533488. The candidate uses bit-exact constants (human_player_scale_4096000, human_player_scale_inverse_108000 = 0x1.36B06Ep-17F, human_player_scale_4096, human_player_scale_30).

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The retail getter returns its value in ST0; the multiplies are 80-bit and each store is `fstp dword`. The candidate multiplies in long double and casts once to float at the store. Index 6 uses `fistp qword` and keeps the low dword; the candidate uses std::rintl (rounds under the current x87 control word, exactly like fistp) followed by the 64-to-32-bit truncation.

checks.name: global_writes
checks.rationale: Retail writes the nine dwords 0x0056E1E8, 0x0056E1EC, 0x0056E1F0, 0x0056E1F4, 0x0056E1F8, 0x0056E1FC, 0x0056E200, 0x0056E204 and 0x0056E208 (the last is index 8 at 0x00410137, not a copy of index 0) and the first dword of each 0x10-byte record in 0x005389F8..0x00538A08 and 0x00538B08..0x00538C18. The candidate writes exactly those 43 dwords into relocated storage with the same layout and writes nothing else.

checks.name: return_block
checks.rationale: Retail builds {+0x00 int32 1, +0x04 unwritten, +0x08 float64 1.0, +0x10 type descriptor 0x00567C74, +0x14 unwritten} and copies six dwords to the first argument with rep movsd. The candidate builds the same block and copies 24 bytes to its context argument; the +0x04 dword is explicitly zero where retail copies stack residue.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: The native has one return path (0x004101AD-0x004101B5) and the candidate has one; both return the first argument in EAX.

differences: The +0x04 dword of the returned block is written as zero by the candidate; retail never writes it and copies whatever the stack held.

The candidate emits `fistp` through std::rintl, so the compiler adds a control-word save, `frndint` and a restore around the conversion; the rounded result is identical under round-to-nearest (the startup control word) and under retail's chop mode (set at 0x00498460 before the task loop).
The candidate's table-B base set-up is folded into the table-B block (see the structural comparison).
status_limits: Static and structural evidence only. No paired retail/candidate runtime capture was made, and the unit is not part of the linked candidate image.
